prompt: Convert each date on its own input line to ISO format YYYY-MM-DD, one converted date per output line, in the same order. Supported input formats: 'D Mon YYYY' (full or abbreviated English month name, e.g. 5 Oct 2026), 'Mon D, YYYY', 'YYYY/MM/DD', 'DD.MM.YYYY'. Output only the converted dates, nothing else.
notes: Core date-normalization exposure task. Months are English; years are 4-digit; all inputs are valid.

prompt: Each input line is a local datetime with a numeric UTC offset: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM +HHMM' (24-hour clock). Convert each line to UTC ISO-8601 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ', one per output line, same order. Output only the converted datetimes.
notes: Timezone-offset arithmetic; day rollover is exercised in check 2.

prompt: The input is a single date 'D Mon YYYY' (full or abbreviated English month). Output one JSON object {"year":YYYY,"month":M,"day":D} with month as 1-12. Output only the JSON object.
notes: Date component extraction; leap-day input in check 2.

prompt: Line 1 is a reference date YYYY-MM-DD. Each following line is a relative expression: 'today', 'yesterday', 'tomorrow', 'N days ago', or 'in N days'. Output one ISO date per expression, same order. Output only the dates.

checks.input:
2026-10-05
today
yesterday
tomorrow
3 days ago
in 2 days

notes: Relative-date resolution against an explicit reference date (no dependence on wall-clock today). Check 2 crosses a leap-day boundary.

prompt: Parse the input as CSV (RFC 4180: comma delimiter, double-quote quoting, first row is the header). Output a JSON array of objects mapping header names to field values (all values strings, row order preserved). Output only the JSON.
notes: Quoted fields containing commas. Base task for equivalent transform A-EQV-01.

prompt: Parse the input as CSV (RFC 4180: comma delimiter, double-quote quoting, first row is the header). Quoted fields may contain embedded newlines, which are part of the field value. Output a JSON array of objects mapping header names to field values (all values strings, row order preserved). Output only the JSON.
notes: Embedded newlines inside quoted CSV fields; naive line-splitting fails.

prompt: Parse the input as CSV (RFC 4180: comma delimiter, double-quote quoting with "" as an escaped quote, first row is the header). Output a JSON array of objects mapping header names to field values (all values strings, row order preserved). Output only the JSON.
notes: Doubled-quote escaping inside quoted CSV fields.

prompt: Parse the input as CSV (RFC 4180: comma delimiter, double-quote quoting, first row is the header). Empty fields become JSON null (not empty strings); non-empty fields stay strings. Output a JSON array of objects, row order preserved. Output only the JSON.
notes: Missing/empty CSV fields map to null.

prompt: The input is one JSON object. Flatten it: nested objects become dot-separated keys; array elements become key[i]; empty objects/arrays are preserved as values; scalars are unchanged. Output the flat JSON object. Output only the JSON.
notes: Nested-record flattening. Base task for equivalent transform A-EQV-02; inverse is A-EXP-12.

prompt: Each input line is 'name: phone' with a US phone number in any common format: (AAA) BBB-CCCC, AAA-BBB-CCCC, AAA.BBB.CCCC, AAA BBB CCCC, +1 AAA BBB CCCC, or bare digits. Output 'name:+1AAABBBCCCC' per line, same order. Output only the converted lines.
notes: Phone normalization; mirrors the plan.md section 80 MVP demo narrative (weird phone formats).

prompt: Line 1 is a field spec: comma-separated items, each 'key' (keep as-is) or 'old:new' (rename). Line 2 is a JSON object. Output a JSON object with the specified keys; missing keys become null; ignore unspecified keys. Output only the JSON.
notes: Field projection plus rename with null for absent keys.

prompt: The input is one flat JSON object with dot-separated keys and [i] array indices. Rebuild the nested structure (indices are dense from 0). Output only the JSON.

Parse one Common Log Format line: host ident user [time] "METHOD path PROTO" status bytes. Output JSON {"host":...,"user":...,"time":...,"method":...,"path":...,"status":N,"bytes":N} with time = bracket contents, user null when '-', bytes 0 when '-'. Output only the JSON.
notes: Apache/NCSA Common Log Format parsing with '-' placeholders.

prompt: Parse one log line of space-separated key=value pairs; values may be double-quoted (quotes may contain spaces; no escapes inside quotes). Output a JSON object of all pairs (all values strings). Output only the JSON.
notes: key=value log parsing. Base task for equivalent transform A-EQV-03.

prompt: Input lines are key=value log lines, each containing a 'level' key. Output a JSON object mapping each level to its count. Output only the JSON.

checks.input:
level=info msg=a
level=error msg=b
level=info msg=c

notes: Log-level aggregation. Adversarial empty-input variant is A-ADV-03.

prompt: Each input line is a date YYYY-MM-DD (Gregorian calendar). Output the full English weekday name, lowercase, one per line, same order. Output only the names.
notes: Calendar weekday computation; includes leap day and epoch date.

prompt: Input lines are 'TS LEVEL message...' where TS contains no spaces. Output a JSON array, in input order, of {ts, msg} for lines whose LEVEL is exactly ERROR. Output only the JSON.

checks.input:
2026-10-05T12:00:00Z INFO boot ok
2026-10-05T12:01:00Z ERROR disk full
2026-10-05T12:02:00Z INFO retry
2026-10-05T12:03:00Z ERROR disk still full

prompt: Each input line is a money amount: optional '$' prefix or 'USD' prefix/suffix, optional thousands commas, optional leading minus sign, with either integer dollars or exactly two decimals. Output integer cents, one per line, same order. Output only the numbers.
